Byomkesh.description: The main detective, known for his sharp intellect and keen observation skills; often referred to respectfully as Byomkeshbabu.

Ajit.description: Byomkesh's close friend and chronicler, who narrates the story and assists in investigations.

Rashomoy Sirkar.description: A wealthy and respected jeweller whose priceless necklace is stolen; he seeks Byomkesh's help to solve the case.

Monimoy Sirkar.description: Rashomoy's elder son, who helps manage the family business and is involved in the events surrounding the theft.

Bhola.description: Rashomoy's personal valet, a canny and wiry man suspected of involvement in the theft.

Amareshbabu.description: The chief inspector at the local police station, known for his toughness and courage; assists in the investigation.

Bhootnath Das.description: Bhola's elder brother, a postal worker who becomes an accomplice in the theft.

Satyaboti.description: Ajit's wife, who appears in domestic scenes and provides comic relief.

Calcutta.description: The major Indian city (now Kolkata) where the story is set.

Bowbazaar.description: A historic neighborhood in central Calcutta, known for its markets and residential areas.

Bombay.description: The former name of Mumbai, a major city in western India.

Madras.description: The former name of Chennai, a major city in southern India.

Rajasthan.description: A large state in northwestern India, mentioned in the context of a royal wedding.

Mechhuabazaar.description: A locality in Calcutta where Bhola's brothers live.

The Sports Club.description: A local club near Rashomoy's house, frequented by Monimoy.

Golap Colony.description: A location referenced in connection with a previous investigation.

Pramod Barat.description: A police officer mentioned as a friend of Amareshbabu and a previous investigator.

Yale lock.description: A type of lock with an automatic latch mechanism, referenced for security in the house.

Cadillac.description: A luxury American car brand, used here to indicate Rashomoy's wealth.

Persian-style tapestries.description: Decorative wall hangings of Persian origin, indicating affluence.

555 cigarettes.description: A popular brand of cigarettes in India, offered to guests in the story.

namaskar.description: A traditional Indian greeting, performed by joining the palms together.

babu.description: A respectful suffix or form of address for men in Bengali and Hindi.

ma.description: A Bengali and Hindi term for mother.

valet.description: A personal attendant or servant, especially one who takes care of clothes and personal needs.

dhoti.description: A traditional Indian garment for men, consisting of a long piece of cloth wrapped around the waist and legs.
